bands.1:
Hollowgum Island is wrapped in mist. Giant hollow gum trees rise out of it.

Creatures are everywhere. A Squintle sits so still it looks like a broken branch. A Hunchlet glides from tree to tree. A Hintatoo screeches from the top of a gum.

A Cubbler waddles past. It is a wombat. It leaves a little brown cube on the path.

"It's perfectly square!" Gus gasps. "Cube poo! That's not gross. That's science."

Maxx's base is inside the biggest tree. It has a gold door. A sign says, "MAXX'S RESCUE RANCH. WHERE CREATURES COME TO BE HAPPY!"

A woman in a long coat appears. She holds a huge magnifying glass. An owl sits on her hat.

"Inspector Fennick," she says. "And this is Owlibi."

"You cook badly," she says to Mo. "There is burnt jam on your sleeve."

"What do you call a wombat detective?" asks Mo. "Sherlock Holes!"

Everyone groans. Even the owl.

She looks at you. "You have not been captain for long. Your boots are new."

Then she looks at Wren. "And you have been on a very fancy yacht."

Wren goes stiff. "Lucky guess," she mutters.

"Are Maxx's rescues fake?" you ask.

"I couldn't possibly say," says the Inspector. "But look closely at his videos. Every rescued Creature has the same scratch."

"So he saves the same Creature again and again!" says Indi.

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge first, Captain," she says. "Until then, notice what is missing."

That night, three trucks full of cages drive in. No trucks come out.

"What's missing is Creatures leaving," you whisper.

The Cubbler leaves a trail of cubes. It leads to a tiny door in the roots.

From behind the door, something is crying.

Then a gold light clicks on.
bands.2:
Hollowgum Island is wrapped in thick white mist. Giant gum trees rise out of it, their trunks so hollow that they look like enormous chimneys. The air smells of eucalyptus and wet earth.

Creatures are everywhere. A Squintle sits so still on a branch that it looks like part of the tree. A Hunchlet glides silently from trunk to trunk. High above, a Hintatoo screeches a warning to its flock.

Then a wombat waddles across the path. It's a Cubbler, and it leaves behind a neat brown cube.

Gus drops to his knees. "It's perfectly square!" he gasps. "Cube poo! That's not gross. That's science."

Mo serves gum-leaf pancakes for breakfast. They taste exactly like cough lollies, and Zed's tongue goes numb.

You find Maxx's base inside the biggest hollow gum of all. A shiny gold door has been fitted into its trunk. The sign above it says, "MAXX'S RESCUE RANCH: WHERE CREATURES COME TO BE HAPPY!"

A tall woman in a long coat steps out of the mist. She carries a magnifying glass the size of a frying pan, and an owl is perched on her hat.

"Inspector Fennick," she says. "And this is Owlibi. He was somewhere else the whole time."

She studies each of you in turn. "You cook badly," she tells Mo. "There's burnt jam on your sleeve."

"What do you call a wombat detective?" asks Mo. "Sherlock Holes!"

Everyone groans. Even Owlibi groans.

She turns to you. "You haven't been captain for long. Your boots are new, and you keep checking the map."

Then her eyes land on Wren. "And you have spent time on a very expensive yacht."

Wren goes stiff. "Lucky guess," she mutters.

"Are Maxx's rescues fake?" you ask.

"I couldn't possibly say," replies the Inspector. "But watch his videos closely. Every Creature he rescues has the same scratch on its left wing."

Indi gasps. "So he's not saving lots of Creatures. He's saving the same one, over and over!"

"Will you help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge first, Captain," she says. "Until then, notice what is missing."

That night, Zed keeps watch on the gold door through his binoculars. Three trucks rumble in, stacked with cages. Not a single truck comes out.

"What's missing," you whisper, "is the Creatures leaving."

Then the Cubbler waddles past again, leaving a trail of cubes. It leads to a tiny door, hidden among the roots of the giant gum.

You creep closer. From behind the door, something is crying.

Then a gold light clicks on above your head.

bands.4:
Hollowgum Island is wrapped in thick white mist. Giant gum trees rise out of it like the masts of sunken ships, their trunks so hollow that they look like enormous chimneys. The air smells of eucalyptus, damp earth and something faintly, suspiciously like an old sock.

Creatures are everywhere, once you know how to look. A Squintle sits so motionless on a branch that it looks like part of the tree, until its eyes snap open and glare at you. A Hunchlet glides silently from trunk to trunk, its skin stretched like a kite. High above, a Hintatoo screeches a warning to the rest of its flock, and a hundred white heads turn your way.

Then a wombat waddles across the track. It's a Cubbler, and it leaves behind a neat brown cube.

Gus drops to his knees in the mud. "It's perfectly square!" he gasps, examining it through his magnifying glass. "Cube poo! That's not gross. That's science."

Mo serves gum-leaf pancakes for breakfast. They taste exactly like cough lollies, and Zed's tongue goes numb for an hour, which everyone agrees is an improvement.

You find Maxx's base inside the biggest hollow gum on the island. A shiny gold door has been bolted into its ancient trunk, and gold fairy lights are stapled all around it. The sign above it says, "MAXX'S RESCUE RANCH: WHERE CREATURES COME TO BE HAPPY!"

A tall woman in a long brown coat steps out of the mist without a sound. She carries a magnifying glass the size of a frying pan, and an owl with enormous orange eyes is perched on her hat.

"Inspector Fennick," she says. "And this is Owlibi. Whatever happened, he was somewhere else the whole time."

She studies each of you in turn, the magnifying glass hovering. "You cook, and badly," she tells Mo. "There's burnt jam on your sleeve, and your eyebrows are slightly singed."

Mo grins, not at all offended. "What do you call a wombat detective?" he asks her. "Sherlock Holes!"

Everyone groans. Even Owlibi groans, a long, low hoot of pure disappointment, which Mo takes as a compliment.

She turns to you. "You haven't been captain for very long. Your boots are brand new, and you keep checking the map when you think nobody is looking."

Then her gaze lands on Wren, and it sharpens. "And you have spent a great deal of time aboard a very expensive yacht."

Wren goes stiff as a fence post. "Lucky guess," she mutters.

"Are Maxx's rescues fake?" you ask.

"I couldn't possibly say," replies the Inspector, polishing her glass. "But I would watch his videos very closely. Every Creature he rescues has exactly the same scratch on its left wing. Draw your own conclusions."

Indi flips open her sketchbook and draws the scratch from memory. It is the same jagged line every time, like a lightning bolt. "So he isn't rescuing lots of Creatures," she says slowly. "He's rescuing the same one, over and over again."

The Inspector says nothing at all, which somehow feels like a yes.

"So you'll help us?" you ask.

"Win my badge first, Captain. I only help people who can read what isn't written down." She tips her hat, and Owlibi blinks slowly. "Until then, notice what is missing."

That night, Zed keeps watch on the gold door through his binoculars, while Tully records everything he sees in her notebook, complete with a tally chart. Three trucks rumble up the muddy track, stacked high with cages. Each one disappears through the gold door. Not a single truck comes out.

"What's missing," you whisper, as the penny drops, "is the Creatures leaving."

Then the Cubbler waddles past again, leaving a fresh trail of cubes behind it like breadcrumbs in a fairy tale. The trail leads to a tiny door, hidden among the knotted roots of the giant gum, so small that you would never have spotted it without a wombat's help.

You creep closer, holding your breath. From behind the door, something is crying.

Then a gold light clicks on above your head.
